Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 01 s. 2023 January 04, 2023 ATTY. MARX EARVIN C. TORINO Legal Officer Ill City Legal Department, Cavite City Province of Cavite Dear Atty. Torino: This has reference to your letter dated November 21 , 2022 seeking legal opinion from this Department on the following: l. Whether reclamation projects are within the powers of the city government; 2. Whether the city government may reclaim lands within their territorial jurisdiction to the exclusion of the provincial government; 3. Whether the provincial govemment may pursue reclamation projects of lands belonging to the city government. If so, may the provincial govemment do so without any participation of the city. per your letter, it is the understanding of the Cavite City government that the city enjoys the same powers granted unto the province under Section 17 of the Local Government Code. It is posited that reclamation projects are embraced by the phrase "all services and facilities of the province" under the same section. Also, you represented that since the City has its own corporate existence and enjoys local autonomy, it may initiate reclamation projects of lands belonging to its territorial boundaries without the provincial govemment's involvement. Hence, the queries. The Department shall answer the queries in seriatim. As to the we answer in the affirmative. Please be apprised that Section 17 (4) provides that a city may exercise the power of reclamation, to wit: Section 17. Basic Services and Facilities. — (a) Local govemment units shall endeavor to be self-reliant and shall continue exercising the powers and discharging the duties and functions currently vested upon them. They "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

shall also discharge the functions and responsibilities of national agencies and offices devolved to them pursuant to this Code. Local govemment units shall likewise exercise such other powers and discharge such other functions and responsibilities as are necessary, appropriate, or incidental to efficient and effective provisions of the basic services and facilities enumerated herein. (b) Such basic services and facilities include, but are not limited to, the following: (3) For a Province: (vii) Infrastructure facilities intended to service the needs of the residence of the province and which are funded out of provincial funds including, but not limited to, provincial roads and bridges; inter-municipal waterworks, drainage and sewerage, flood control, and irrigation systems; reclamation projects; and similar facilities; 4) For a City: All the services and facilities of the municipality and province, and in addition thereto, the following: xxxx (Emphasis and underlining supplied) From the above-cited section, a city may exercise such other powers and discharge other functions and responsibilities as are necessary, appropriate, or incidental to efficient and effective provisions of the basic services and facilities of a province. Verily, a city may also exercise reclamation projects as embraced by the phrase "all services and facilities of the province" under the said section. The words of the LGC are unambiguous and need no interpretation that reclamation projects are within the powers of a city. However, the Department of Justice opined in Opinion No. 93, S. 1993 dated July 26, 1993, that the extent of the authority granted to Philippine Reclamation Authority under PD 1084 and EO 525, which are special laws, has not been reduced with the subsequent enactment of the 1991 Local Govemment Code, which is a general law. The authority of the local government units, specifically provinces and cities, to undertake reclamation projects are limited to those projects funded out of local funds. As to the gæng_gug.m this Level answers in the affirmative. May we invite your attention to the Administrative Order No. 20194 (AO) of the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA). Section 4 of said AO specifically provides: Section 4. Requirements for the processing of applications to reclaim The following requirements shall be submitted for evaluation prior to the approval of the reclaim projects/reclamation components by the PRA Governing Board: Page 2 of 4

4.1 Pre-Qualification Requirements The following are the Pre-Qualification requirements for all application for reclamation project/components: 4.1.1 Legal Requirements a. Letter of Intent (LOI) from Applicant b. Provincial/City Council Resolutions expressing no objection to the proposed reclamation project e. For LGUs/GOCCs1NGAs i. Certified True Copy of the Council's xxxx Resolution authorizing LGU xxx to file an application with PRA; ii. Certified True Copy of the charter or other incorporation documents; and iii. Certified True Copy of Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) Certificate of Registration. 4.1.2 Financial Requirements c. For LGUs/GOCCs/NGAs i. Certified True Copy of the Audited Financial Statements for the past three years; ii. Certified True Copy of the Income tax Retum (ITR) for the past three years; and iii. BIR Tax Clearance Certificate. Section 4 of the above-cited AO laid down the requirements for the processing of reclamation, and nowhere in the said section requires the need for the authorization from the provincial govemment for a city to exercise its reclamation power. What is required is only the Sanggunian Panlungsod's Resolution expressing no objection to the proposed reclamation project. Moreover, the approval of the reclamation project is within the PRA's authority, not with the provincial govemment, as long as the requirements are duly complied with. Also, we are of the view that since Cities also have reclamation powers as given by the LGC, cities enjoy local autonomy regarding their exercise of reclamation powers within their territorial jurisdiction with the exclusion of the provincial govemment. Thus, the reclamation power of the city may be exercised to the exclusion of the provincial government since the latter's power is merely supervisory over cities to ensure that their acts are within the scope of their prescribed powers and functions. With regard to the last query, we opine in the negative if the reclamation was pursued by the province without the permission of the city pursuant to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Administrative Order No. 2018-141. 1 SECTION 8.
